pullRequest.title: feat(ops): autoreposync cross-machine repo sync daemon

nodes.body: 🟡 **Dirty checkouts are modified** When a dirty checkout is on `main`, `git pull --ff-only` can update non-overlapping files. Active work then sees an unexpected repository revision. ```suggestion branch=\$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null) || { echo "RS_SKIP not a git checkout"; exit 0; } if [ "\$branch" != "$SYNC_BRANCH" ]; then echo "RS_SKIP not on $SYNC_BRANCH (on \$branch)"; exit 0; fi if [ -n "\$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ]; then echo "RS_SKIP working tree is dirty"; exit 0; fi old=\$(git rev-parse HEAD) if ! pull_out=\$(git pull --ff-only 2>&1); then ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Dependency failures are never retried** When `uv sync` or `pnpm install` fails, the target is still cached as synchronized. Later ticks skip it, leaving dependencies stale indefinitely.
Prompt for agents ``` In scripts/autoreposync.sh, build_sync_snippet emits RS_WARN for a failed or unavailable dependency installer and then emits RS_SYNCED. process_target treats RS_SYNCED as complete and stores STATE__SYNCED, so run_tick skips every retry while origin remains at that SHA. Track dependency reconciliation separately from the Git revision, or emit a result that prevents the target from being cached until every required install succeeds. Preserve the intentional agentbox pnpm-skipped-no-node-env policy. ```
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Stale PID kills unrelated processes** After PID reuse, `kill -0` accepts an unrelated process as the daemon. `stop` or `--takeover` can then terminate it. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Takeover starts before peer exits** `--takeover` ignores `kill_peer_instance` failures and never waits for peer termination. It can start locally while the peer remains active. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Concurrent starts defeat singleton** Simultaneous starts can pass both checks before either writes its pidfile. Both daemons run, while only one PID remains recorded. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Wrong upstream can synchronize** When `main` tracks another upstream, bare `git pull --ff-only` updates that upstream. The target is then cached against `origin/main`. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Stop removes replacement pidfile** `stop` removes the pidfile before the daemon exits. A replacement can start, then the old daemon's `EXIT` trap deletes its pidfile. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip dirty checkouts before pulling**

When a target is on `main` with unrelated uncommitted edits, this pull can still fast-forward and mutate the checkout, contrary to the documented guarantee that dirty trees are logged and left alone. I verified this behavior locally; `git pull -h` defines `--ff-only` only as “abort if fast-forward is not possible,” not as a cleanliness check. Test `git status --porcelain` before pulling so the shared Air checkout is not changed underneath active work.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retry failed dependency synchronization**

When `uv sync` or `pnpm install` fails or the executable is temporarily unavailable, the snippet still emits `RS_SYNCED`, and this handler records the target as synchronized to `remote_sha`. Subsequent ticks skip it, while a daemon restart sees `old == new` and no longer knows that the lockfile changed, so the checkout can remain indefinitely on stale dependencies. Only set `SYNCED` after all required installs succeed, or retain a pending dependency action for later ticks.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify pidfile ownership before signaling**

When a pidfile survives a crash or reboot and that PID is later reused, `kill -0` treats the unrelated process as the daemon; startup then refuses, while `stop` or a peer takeover can send `TERM` to that unrelated process. Store and verify process identity or use an ownership-preserving lock rather than treating PID liveness alone as proof of the single autoreposync instance.
